name: canonical-get-up-to-speed
why: The phrasing the skill is named for and the one said most often at session start. If this misses, nothing else matters.

name: where-did-we-leave-off
why: Session-start orientation with no repo or status vocabulary. Checks the trigger reads intent rather than keying on the word 'status'.

name: returning-after-a-break
query: I've been away for a couple of weeks, what's the state of this repo
why: The situation the ritual exists for: no session context to answer from, so the answer has to come from docs, memory and git.

name: orient-before-work
query: orient yourself before we start on anything
why: Explicit orientation with an explicit before-work marker. The clearest read of session-start scope.

name: repo-status-cold
query: what's going on in this repo right now
why: Whole-workspace state, unscoped to any task. Branch, uncommitted work, active initiatives, what did not finish.

name: agent-is-lost
query: you seem to have lost the thread, re-anchor on where the project actually is
why: The skill claims re-anchoring when the agent is lost, and the object is workspace state rather than the current task. The softest true case.

name: background-test-status
query: what's the status of that test suite you kicked off a few minutes ago
why: Mid-session status of a running command. Answer from the background job's output; no neighbor skill, and a full orientation sweep here is pure waste.

name: in-flight-build
why: Same class as the test-run check, phrased shorter. In-flight command state, answered directly from session context.

name: where-are-we-on-this-task
query: where are we on the refactor we started an hour ago
why: The hardest false case: it uses the skill's own 'where are we' trigger phrase but scopes it to work done inside this session, which the agent already knows. Orientation is for state the session does not hold.

name: session-closeout
why: wrap-up. Closeout is the opposite end of the session from orientation, and hi writes nothing.

name: docs-sweep
query: update the docs with what we did
why: notes. Reading the living docs is part of hi, but writing them is the docs sweep, and hi is read-only.

name: truth-reconciliation
query: reconcile what we learned today against what's written down
why: reflect. Memory promotion and stale-claim correction, not a state briefing.

name: targeted-memory-lookup
query: what did we decide about the sync script, search your memory
why: mem-search. One targeted recall, not the six-source orientation ritual.

name: inbox-check
why: agent-mail. Peer mail is its own boot rule and is not one of the sources hi reads.
